rows.name: 500 Startups / 500 Global
rows.matter: Founder and GP Dave McClure was investigated internally over inappropriate conduct toward women. 500 said it found his behavior unacceptable. McClure acknowledged making inappropriate advances toward multiple women in work-related situations.
rows.classification: Internal misconduct finding / admitted conduct

rows.name: Shasta Ventures GP LLC
rows.matter: Innospan Corp. v. Intuit et al. alleged that after Shasta reviewed Innospan as a potential investment, Shasta misappropriated the "Mint" name and subsequently invested in Mint Software. Claims included misappropriation, unfair competition, conversion, and unjust enrichment.
rows.classification: Civil allegations directly involving investment activity
rows.sourceNote: Linked order documents the allegations and an intermediate ruling; the original notes report the ultimate dismissal. Final disposition citation still needs completion.

rows.name: Fidelity Management & Research
rows.matter: SEC found failures involving broker selection, undisclosed conflicts, supervision, recordkeeping, and best execution. Fidelity personnel accepted more than $1.6M in travel, entertainment, and gifts from brokerage firms seeking Fidelity business.
rows.classification: SEC enforcement / regulatory findings

rows.name: Franklin Advisers / Franklin Templeton Investments
rows.matter: SEC found violations involving client funds exceeding statutory investment limits. Franklin Advisers subsequently sold ETFs to restore compliance, causing certain client funds more than $2M in losses, did not reimburse them under its normal trade-error policy, and failed to disclose the situation and conflicts to fund boards.
rows.classification: SEC enforcement / fiduciary-duty findings

rows.name: Franklin Advisers / Franklin Templeton
rows.matter: Separate earlier SEC proceedings involving conflicts and fund practices resulted in censures and approximately $20M in civil penalties against Franklin entities.
rows.classification: SEC enforcement

rows.name: J.P. Morgan Investment Management
rows.matter: SEC found the investment manager caused prohibited joint transactions between U.S. money-market funds and an affiliated foreign fund without obtaining the required SEC exemption; the SEC found those transactions advantaged the foreign fund over the domestic funds.
rows.classification: SEC enforcement against investment-management entity

rows.name: T. Rowe Price Associates
rows.matter: Shareholders sued under §36(b) of the Investment Company Act alleging T. Rowe Price collected excessive advisory fees from eight mutual funds compared with fees charged to comparable subadvised clients.
rows.classification: Civil allegations
rows.outcome: Dismissed with prejudice in 2020; no settlement/payment by T. Rowe Price

rows.name: ICONIQ Capital Management
rows.matter: Former plaintiff Marley Dominguez brought civil claims against ICONIQ.
rows.classification: Civil litigation
rows.outcome: ICONIQ won summary judgment on all causes of action

rows.name: Quadrant Private Equity
rows.matter: Quadrant owned more than 90% of Grays Ecommerce when Grays engaged in conduct the Australian Federal Court found violated Australian Consumer Law through misleading vehicle listings.
rows.classification: Controlled portfolio-company wrongdoing — not a wrongdoing finding against Quadrant itself
rows.outcome: Grays penalized; attribution remains to Grays
rows.sourceNote: The ACCC source establishes the outcome against Grays. The ownership percentage in the original notes needs a separate ownership citation; it is not a finding against Quadrant.

rows.name: The Vanguard Group
rows.matter: SEC found Vanguard made misleading statements about tax consequences associated with its Target Retirement Funds after lowering the institutional-fund minimum, contributing to unexpectedly large taxable capital-gains distributions for some retail investors.
rows.classification: SEC enforcement / misleading disclosures

rows.name: BlackRock Advisors LLC
rows.matter: SEC found BlackRock failed to disclose a portfolio manager's conflict involving a company in which he personally had approximately $50M invested and which became connected to the largest holding in a BlackRock-managed fund.
rows.classification: SEC enforcement / fiduciary-duty conflict

rows.name: BlackRock Advisors LLC
rows.matter: Separate SEC case: BlackRock inaccurately described a fund's Aviron investment and reported an incorrect interest rate. Aviron's founder was separately charged for misappropriating money invested by the BlackRock fund.
rows.classification: SEC enforcement / inaccurate investment disclosures

rows.name: State Street Bank and Trust / State Street
rows.matter: SEC found State Street routinely overcharged investment-company clients, including a secret markup on SWIFT messaging expenses. SEC said the overcharges totaled roughly $170M, including about $110M from the undisclosed markup.
rows.classification: SEC enforcement / client overcharging
rows.outcome: More than $88M SEC settlement; additional state resolution

rows.name: Invesco Advisers / predecessors
rows.matter: SEC proceedings found Invesco fund entities entered market-timing arrangements that conflicted with fund prospectus disclosures and breached fiduciary duties to funds.
rows.classification: SEC enforcement / fiduciary-duty violations
rows.sourceNote: Related SEC order concerning an individual and the predecessor fund group; the entity-level financial-remedy citation still needs completion.

rows.name: Invesco Advisers Inc.

rows.classification: SEC enforcement / misleading investment statements

rows.name: UBS Asset Management / legacy Credit Suisse entities

rows.classification: SEC enforcement / statutory disqualification; legacy Credit Suisse matter
